scenario_provenance.archetype_label: Multi-focus on Practices 3 & 4 (analyze data; interpret results)
validity_rules: one chance process or one selected unit defines the trial
mutually exclusive means no single outcome can satisfy both event definitions
overlapping events have at least one shared outcome and are not mutually exclusive

sources.note: the item stem's verb must match the scored demand

prompt: For one card selected from a standard deck, let Event A be that the card is red and Event B be that the card is a spade. Which statement best justifies whether Events A and B are mutually exclusive?

options.text: The events are mutually exclusive, because the two descriptions use different labels for the selected outcome.

misconception_source.label: Assumed different labels make events disjoint

sources.note: mutual exclusivity is about shared outcomes, not whether event names are different

options.text: The events are not mutually exclusive, because over many repetitions of the chance process one event could occur on one trial and the other could occur on another trial.

sources.note: the relationship is determined within a single chance process or selected observational unit

options.text: The events are mutually exclusive, because a spade is black, so one selected card cannot be both red and a spade.
The events are independent, because if Event A occurs, then Event B cannot also occur.

sources.note: mutually exclusive events have no outcomes in common; distinguish this from independence

parts.prompt: For one card selected from a standard deck, let Event A be that the card is red and Event B be that the card is a spade. Which statement best justifies whether Events A and B are mutually exclusive?

criteria.description: Selects the justification that correctly identifies whether the two events can occur on the same trial.
criteria.required_evidence: The events are mutually exclusive, because a spade is black, so one selected card cannot be both red and a spade.
